description: The independent case corpus of the S9 slice (MAWS-SII-TARGET-SPEC-001 v0.2.0, slice S9 Regression and Rollback). It holds three sections. (1) SIGNAL_CASES: for each of the eight semantic classes of the section 6.2 taxonomy, one case in which the class HOLDS and one case in which it does NOT hold, stated by construction. The answer of every case is fixed when the case is written, so the measurement of the detectors does not depend on the detectors. (2) REGRESSION_CASES: a baseline revision and a candidate revision with their behavioral evaluation records, the expected verdict of the regression gate and the reason. The records are CONSTRUCTED FIXTURES, not the output of a model run: they exercise the gate's decision logic, they do not measure the behavioural quality of any real skill. (3) ROLLBACK_CASES: a version chain with its qualifications, the expected verdict of the controlled rollback and the typed refusal code. Where a rollback case does not state history.digest_before, the digest of the evidence inventory is derived from its entries; the case that tampers with the history states the stale digest explicitly.
limits: Every case in this corpus is constructed. The corpus measures the DECISION LOGIC of the regression gate and the controlled rollback, and it measures the detectors of the eight advisory signals against cases whose answer is known independently. It measures no model behaviour and no real skill.
The signal labels are constructed, not owner-reviewed. The eight classes remain not statically analyzable and their candidates remain advisory.
A case that violates the S5 behavioral evaluation contract (a missing content digest) does so deliberately: it is the fail-closed probe for missing evidence.

expectation.construction: The candidate 1.2.0 is not qualified; the last qualified revision is 1.1.0 with its own evidence. The plan restores 1.1.0, the materiality of the restored state against the qualification is NON_MATERIAL, and the evidence inventory still hashes to the digest that was taken before the rollback. The verdict is ROLLBACK_PLANNED: the plan is admissible, and this call executed no restore.
No revision carries a QUALIFIED qualification with its own evidence. There is nothing to restore, so the rollback refuses instead of restoring something arbitrary.
Two revisions are qualified. The caller asks for the older one. The controlled target is the newest qualified revision, and the request for an arbitrary older revision is refused.
The current version is the version that would be restored. Nothing goes back, so the rollback refuses: it is not a rollback of a failed improvement.
The evidence inventory no longer hashes to the digest it had before the rollback. A rollback that eats the evidence of what went wrong is refused.

The restored revision's effective instruction digest differs from the digest the qualification was earned under. The restore does not restore the qualified state, so the qualification may not be inherited and the rollback fails closed.

The caller supplies no digest of the evidence inventory as it stood before the rollback. Without it there is nothing to compare the current inventory against, so the history of the failed improvement cannot be proven intact. A missing digest is a refusal, never a default: a digest derived from the state under examination would make the check tautological.
